title: Hierarchical responsiveness and modal priority heuristics for Console dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Console pages (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) show increased layout complexity: dense tables, large interactive charts, and stacked modals. On narrow viewports and under heavy touch interactions we see layout jank, gesture conflicts, and canvas clipping leading to poor perceived performance. Goal: define a hierarchy-driven responsiveness system that decides which UI surface reduces density, which elements collapse or float, and how modals/panels get priority for interaction. Deliverables: detailed interaction heuristics, cross-browser fallbacks, responsive CSS/Container Query guidelines, touch/gesture precedence rules, and a working Figma prototype with annotated flows and QA checklist.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Console pages adapt for three canonical widths (>=1280, 720-1279, <720) with documented element priority rules
A2: Modal stacking behavior defined: primary modal keeps focus+drag gesture while secondary modals degrade to drawers or full-screen sheets on small viewports
A3: Chart canvases provide a visual fallback (SVG sparklines or low-res raster) when GPU memory or Safari painting issues are detected
A4: Tables use column-priority collapse rules with a compact row variant and virtualization for >200 rows
A5: Cross-browser notes included for Safari (sticky headers), Firefox (scroll anchoring), and Chromium (composited transforms), with test matrix
A6: Prototype validated in design review and sign-off from PM and Eng owners

decisions: Decision 1: Use a hierarchical priority list per page: primary surface (chart/table), secondary controls (filters/toolbar), tertiary supplemental panels (details, tooltips). Compression order will follow this list.
Decision 2: Modal degradation rule: on small viewports, secondary modals convert to bottom sheets; tertiary overlays become transient toasts with action links.
Decision 3: Default to container queries for component sizing; include CSS custom properties for runtime tuning by Eng.
Decision 4: Implement chart fallback using progressive enhancement: canvas -> SVG -> static raster depending on browser capability and memory signals.
next_steps: Finalize CSS pattern library tokens and container query examples (owner: Design)
Create engineering RFC with runtime flag proposals and perf guardrails (owner: Eng)
Prototype touch gesture precedence in a lightweight web demo and run on iOS Safari and Android Chrome (owner: Design+Eng)
Add QA matrix rows for cross-browser painting and sticky header regressions (owner: QA)
qa_notes: Test 1: Resize stress test from 1600px down to 360px, verify content priority retained for primary surface
Test 2: Safari iOS 16 painting test with large charts open; verify fallback triggers without blocking interaction
Test 3: Keyboard navigation across degraded modals must trap focus in primary modal only
Test 4: Memory pressure simulation with many open charts to ensure fallback path engages
accessibility_considerations: Ensure role and aria changes when a modal converts to sheet/full-screen
Maintain focus order and visible focus rectangle after layout changes
Provide non-visual announcements when content collapses or columns hide
Avoid relying solely on color for important state changes in compact mode
